A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 40-page PRDP paper, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical scientific content; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp and document metadata.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Poisson inverse-problem and PDE emulator experiments. Appendix G reports measured training times, validation errors and ablations.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, including Figure 24's training times, Table 1's validation errors and Figures 25–26's ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 4 retain identical refinement steps, plateau detection, stopping criteria and treatment of implicit and unrolled differentiation.

E1.justification: Evaluated coverage remains Poisson inverse problems, heat diffusion emulation in 1D/2D/3D, 1D Burgers emulation and 2D Navier–Stokes neural-hybrid correction. No datasets or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same fully converged-physics baselines, fixed-refinement comparisons and manually scheduled Poisson comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F report identical validation metrics, data generation and splits, model configurations, solver settings and training procedures.

E4.justification: The network-size ablation in Appendix G.3 and validation-error versus training-loss refinement study in Appendix G.4 are identical. The main-text refinement and solver/differentiation analyses also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten seeds affecting network initialization and stochastic minibatching, mean curves with one-standard-deviation shading, and mean ± standard deviation in Table 1.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match, including Table 1's validation errors and Section 4.4's reported 62% Navier–Stokes training-time reduction. No results are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Section 2's mathematical formulation, Appendix B's solver algorithms, Appendix C's differentiation derivations and Appendix D's PDE discretizations are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about adaptive refinement, computational savings from incomplete convergence and applicability across differentiable-physics learning scenarios.

C2.justification: The hypotheses explaining incomplete-convergence savings, Section 6's applicability limits and Appendix G.4's qualifications about using training loss are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 8 and Appendices D–F retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, data generation instructions and source-code access statement.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to bilevel optimization and earlier approximate-differentiation methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 26 February 2025 to v2 dated 13 November 2025. The paper's wording, headings and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned. All figures, tables, captions and scientific-content layouts, including the appendices, are identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and substantive presentation are identical throughout the main text and appendices. Updating the arXiv stamp and PDF metadata produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
